rendered: The premise does not hold. The document does not report bare Al outperforming the carbon/Al collector. At the high current, bare Al was the weaker electrode: its electrodes were prone to failure at these currents, and the authors attribute the bare Al shorting to uneven plating caused by its higher nucleation overpotential.[1][2] The carbon/Al collector, by contrast, kept a low voltage hysteresis of 45 mV[3] at 4 mA/cm^2[4]. The text gives no hysteresis value for bare Al at that current, so the size of any difference cannot be quantified from this document. The only hysteresis comparison offered is a previous study using Cu electrodes, which reported nearly double the hysteresis[5] at that current. Bare Al's failure at these currents is only cited as supplementary Figure S3, which is not shown here.
